_status: DRAFT, NOT IMPORTED. Tunisia is the third of three North Africa countries researched this session (AF/G.9 priority 1) -- Algeria and Morocco alongside it. Researched by a subagent this session against the branch's full Research.1.md discipline, reading INS's own methodology brief directly plus the operative pension statutes for both CNRPS (public) and CNSS (private). Sitting in src/data/research/ pending Thomas's review, following the established DRAFT-then-import pattern.
_note: Tunisia is the third and clearest North Africa confirmation of a now-familiar branch pattern: real, statutory, non-CPI benefit-adjustment mechanisms rather than either an explicit denial or plain silence. The CNRPS (public-sector) pension statute automatically re-adjusts pensions whenever the retiree's civil-service pay grade rises ('péréquation'); the CNSS (private-sector) decree automatically revalues pensions in payment at every increase in the SMIG (minimum wage). Both are corroborated independently by the ISSA and SSA/ISSA country profiles, which each state plainly: 'Not legally mandated. Indexed based on changes in the legal minimum wage.' Tunisia's flagship cash-transfer programme, PNAFN, shows a third shape again: no formula of any kind was found in any document reviewed, CPI-based or otherwise -- its benefit level has moved through a documented series of discrete ad hoc increases (TND 7.7 in 1987 to TND 180 in 2020) that an academic working paper compares only to the minimum wage, never to the CPI. On the CPI itself, Tunisia is confirmed on the IMF's stronger SDDS dissemination tier -- directly quoted from the IMF's own 2024 Annual Observance Report -- with a documented, quoted timeliness lapse in practice attributed to a December 2024 SDMX platform migration, worth noting as a genuine deviation rather than smoothed over.

_open_questions.question: INS's methodology brief names 'COICOP' with a 12-division structure matching the pre-2018 vintage, not the restructured COICOP 2018. The `un-coicop-2018` edge below should be treated as approximate pending a document that states the exact vintage Tunisia applies.

A secondary source (finco.tn) describes SMIG (minimum wage) increases as set via periodic government décret on a multi-year negotiated schedule, and a press commentary piece (webmanagercenter.com) states increases run 'toujours en retard sur l'inflation réelle' (always lagging behind actual inflation) -- both consistent with no automatic CPI-indexation of the SMIG itself, but the underlying Journal Officiel décret text was not reached directly this session (site access blocked).

An African Development Bank evaluation titled (in French) 'Performance of Tunisia's Social Assistance System and the Challenges of Informality' could not be retrieved this session -- the URL returned a Cloudflare bot-check page on two separate attempts. Its title suggests it may contain directly relevant material on PNAFN benefit adequacy.

Unlike Tanzania, Malawi and Eswatini (each of which has a titled national social-protection strategy/policy document explicitly discussing benefit adequacy vs. inflation), no equivalent Tunisian Ministry of Social Affairs strategy document was located this session -- only press commentary. Worth a further search specifically on social.gov.tn.

reports.title: Indice des Prix à la Consommation Familiale, Base 100 en 2015
reports.publisher: Institut National de la Statistique (INS), Tunisia
reports.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session via INS's own methodology brief. 'L'INS a finalisé la confection d'un nouvel indice des prix à la consommation familiale (IPC) base 100 en 2015, en remplacement de l'ancien indice base 100 en 2010.' Formula: elementary aggregates via 'la formule de Jevons' (geometric mean), higher-level aggregation via 'la formule de Laspeyres.' Classification: 'La classification des fonctions de consommation des ménages (Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose - COICOP)... comporte 12 fonctions' -- version unstated, structure matches the pre-2018 vintage (see _open_questions). The full 6-page brief was searched for 'FMI'/'IMF', 'manuel', 'SNA'/'comptabilité nationale', 'Arabe', 'Maghreb' -- none appear as a compliance statement.

reports.title: Loi n° 85-12 du 5 mars 1985, portant régime des pensions civiles et militaires de retraite et des survivants dans le secteur public
reports.publisher: République Tunisienne / Journal Officiel de la République Tunisienne (JORT)
reports.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session (as amended by Loi n° 2007-43 du 25 juin 2007). Public-sector pension statute administered by the Caisse Nationale de Retraite et de Prévoyance Sociale (CNRPS). Article 37 (nouveau): 'La péréquation de la pension est effectuée lors de toute augmentation de l'un quelconque des éléments permanents de la rémunération correspondante au grade ou à la fonction sur la base de laquelle a été liquidée la pension.' A mandatory but salary-grade-linked mechanism, not CPI-linked; no mention of inflation or a price index anywhere in Articles 35-38 (all read directly).

reports.title: Décret n° 74-499 du 27 avril 1974, relatif au régime de vieillesse, d'invalidité et de survivants dans le secteur non agricole
reports.publisher: République Tunisienne / Journal Officiel de la République Tunisienne (JORT)
reports.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session. Private-sector (non-agricultural) old-age, disability and survivors' pension decree administered by the Caisse Nationale de Sécurité Sociale (CNSS). Article 53 (nouveau): 'Le montant des pensions au cours de paiement est revalorisé automatiquement à chaque augmentation du SMIG.' A mandatory, automatic mechanism tied to the SMIG (minimum wage), not CPI. Also sets a pension floor at '2/3 du SMIG' -- again minimum-wage-referenced, not CPI-referenced.

reports.title: Programme National d'Aide aux Familles Nécessiteuses (PNAFN)
reports.description: Tunisia's flagship non-contributory unconditional cash-transfer programme for needy families, established 1986. Per the World Bank's own Project Information Document (P506533): 'based mainly on unconditional permanent cash transfers (PCT) to households who lack financial and family support, such as the elderly poor and individuals with disabilities.' Per an Economic Research Forum working paper, the monthly benefit has risen through discrete ad hoc increases (TND 7.7 in 1987, TND 36.3 in 2000, TND 56.7 in 2010, TND 105 in 2013, TND 180 in 2020) compared throughout only to the minimum wage (SMIG), never to CPI. No CPI-indexation formula was found in any document reviewed.
